subject: general
question: The respiratory pigment, haemoglobin is present in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**red blood corpuscles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Red Blood Corpuscles (Erythrocytes):**

 
 
• Hemoglobin is a protein contained within red blood corpuscles (erythrocytes).
 
• These cells are the most abundant cells in the blood and are responsible for transporting oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues.
 
• Hemoglobin is the molecule that actually binds to the oxygen.
 
• Each hemoglobin molecule can carry up to four oxygen molecules.
 
• The iron in hemoglobin gives red blood cells their characteristic red color.
 
• Red blood cells are biconcave discs, which increases their surface area for gas exchange.
 
• They lack a nucleus, mitochondria, and other organelles, which allows for more space to accommodate hemoglobin.
 
• Red blood cells are produced in the bone marrow.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **White Blood Corpuscles (Leukocytes):**

 
 
• White blood corpuscles are part of the immune system and help defend the body against infections and diseases.
 
• They are not involved in oxygen transport, and they do not contain hemoglobin.
 
• There are different types of white blood cells, each with specific functions in the immune response.
 
 
 
• **Blood Platelets (Thrombocytes):**
 
 
• Blood platelets are small, irregular cells that play a crucial role in blood clotting (hemostasis).
 
• They are not involved in oxygen transport and do not contain hemoglobin.
 
• When a blood vessel is damaged, platelets clump together to form a plug, helping to stop bleeding.
 
 
 
• **Blood Plasma:**
 
 
• Blood plasma is the liquid component of blood, making up about 55% of its total volume.
 
• It is a straw-colored fluid that carries various substances, including nutrients, hormones, and proteins.
 
• While plasma carries some dissolved oxygen, the vast majority of oxygen in the blood is transported by hemoglobin within red blood cells.
 
• Plasma does not contain hemoglobin itself.
